topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic serves as the opening framing for the lecture, introducing the lecturer, context within the course, and key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore what drives cancer development by evaluating the relative contributions of endogenous cellular processes, environmental exposures, and population-level epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Causes of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, detailing the collaborative role of viral and parasitic infections in the pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens induce DNA damage directly or via metabolic activation into reactive intermediates.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Host Susceptibility, and Mechanistic Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic aspects of carcinogenesis—including the distinction between initiators and promoters, tissue and life-stage susceptibility—and summarize the diversity of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the analytical, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro methods used to identify mutational signatures and evaluate whether substances are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Conclusion: Risk-Benefit Decisions and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing of the lecture, summarizing key takeaways and highlighting how individuals and societies navigate exposure risks.
